run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: Investigated with the app-267-prod-logs index as instructed. The entire index holds 4 documents in the authorized window and every one of them carries cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1, so by its own fields the data belongs to the cluster the question names; the index is the only index present. The four documents form one chain: at 2026-11-23T15:58:18Z checkout-service logged "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)" and payment-service logged "Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms"; at 16:58:18Z checkout-service logged "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)"; at 17:28:18Z payment-service logged, as WARN, "adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620". No other service or Kubernetes object appears in the index. The deepest cause the evidence indicates is the external payment provider adyen-eu, with payment-service upstream timeouts and checkout-service 500s plus circuit-breaker as consequences; the provider itself is outside the cluster and no available source observes it. Counter-evidence from cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 (namespace otel-demo): checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm are Running and ready with 0 restarts, created at 14:36:30Z and 14:36:29Z, with no rollout; checkout stdout shows completed orders ("payment went through") at 16:02-16:09Z and 17:15-17:56Z, and payment stdout shows "Transaction complete." at 17:01-17:08Z and 17:53-17:56Z. The internal fault-injection candidates were checked and are not on: ConfigMap flagd-config defines paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable but both have defaultVariant "off" (off=false / off=0) and flagd-config has not been written since helm applied it at 14:36:29Z. No NetworkPolicies exist, no Ingresses exist, and the checkout and payment Services select the running pods. Jaeger and Prometheus were both unreachable during this Run, so no error rate, span status or latency measurement exists and no latency trend against a baseline can be stated. Also noted: the index's service labels (checkout-service, payment-service) match no workload in this cluster, whose deployments are named checkout and payment, so the failing application instances named in the index were not observable as pods here. Conclusion is partial because the causal chain rests on 4 log documents only, with the external provider and the failing instances themselves unobservable.

claims.text: The index app-267-prod-logs contains exactly 4 documents in the window 2026-10-24T17:58:26Z-2026-11-23T17:58:26Z, all with cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1: ERROR checkout-service 2026-11-23T15:58:18Z "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)"; ERROR payment-service 2026-11-23T15:58:18Z "Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms"; ERROR checkout-service 2026-11-23T16:58:18Z "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)"; WARN payment-service 2026-11-23T17:28:18Z "adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620".

A listing of all indices returns only app-267-prod-logs (status open, health green, docs.count 4), and its mapping has keyword fields cluster, environment, level, region, service and a date field timestamp; searches must use timestamp as the time field.

In cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1, namespace otel-demo, pods checkout-6578865d87-v6flf (owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87, created 2026-11-23T14:36:30Z) and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6, created 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z) are Running and ready with restartCount 0; all 21 otel-demo deployments have replicas=1, ready=1, available=1, updated=1, and the deployment list contains "checkout" and "payment" but no workload named checkout-service or payment-service.

Checkout pod stdout in otel-demo shows completed orders ("[PlaceOrder] ...", "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)", "order confirmation email sent ...") at 16:02:47Z, 16:03:08Z, 16:03:48Z, 16:05:28Z, 16:07:19Z, 16:07:57Z, 16:08:14Z, 16:08:21Z, 16:08:48Z and 16:09:56Z, and continuously from 17:15:43Z through 17:56:27Z.

Payment pod stdout in otel-demo shows "Charge request received." followed by "Transaction complete." with transactionId at 17:01:23Z, 17:02:25Z, 17:02:35Z, 17:02:39Z, 17:03:34Z, 17:04:04Z, 17:04:12Z, 17:04:18Z, 17:04:35Z, 17:04:59Z, 17:05:54Z, 17:06:29Z, 17:06:44Z, 17:07:20Z, 17:08:46Z and again at 17:53:51Z-17:56:27Z.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo defines fault-injection flags paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%", variants 100%=1, 90%=0.95, 75%=0.75, 50%=0.5, 25%=0.25, 10%=0.1, off=0) and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable", on=true, off=false); both are state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off", so the value in effect is off.

ConfigMap flagd-config was last written by manager helm (Apply) at 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z with no later managedFields entry, and the flagd pod log contains only its 14:37:14Z startup lines (version v0.12.8, file resolver watching ./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json, IResolver listening on 8013) with no subsequent flag-change line.

No NetworkPolicy object exists in the cluster and no Ingress object exists; Service payment (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment) and Service checkout (8080 -> 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout) are ClusterIP services whose selectors match the running pods, so no service, endpoint or policy misconfiguration was observed.

The cluster's own checkout and payment application logs do not show the reported failures: checkout completed orders successfully at 16:02-16:09Z, the same period in which the index records a 15:58:18Z checkout POST /api/checkout failure and a 16:58:18Z open circuit breaker, and both pods have restartCount 0 with the same creation time as every other otel-demo pod, so no restart or unchanged-template rollout happened in the window.

The 500s on POST /api/checkout originate at the external payment provider adyen-eu: it took longer than 30s to answer /v68/payments, payment-service's upstream call timed out, checkout-service returned 500 on POST /api/checkout and then opened its circuit breaker for payment-service (36% failure rate), leaving payment-service in degraded mode with a retry queue depth of 620. This rests on the four index documents only; the provider's own state is not observed by any available source.

The failing applications named in the index (checkout-service, payment-service) are instances not observed in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1: the cluster's workloads are named checkout and payment, their sampled stdout shows only successful charges and no adyen-related line, so the index documents may describe a different deployment of the same prod/eu-west-1 environment than the otel-demo pods.

Considered and rejected: that an enabled flagd fault-injection flag caused the payment timeouts. paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are both configured with defaultVariant "off" (off=false / off=0), flagd-config has not been written since helm applied it at 14:36:29Z, and flagd logged no flag change after its 14:37:14Z startup, so no such setting is switched on.

Ask the payment provider for its adyen-eu /v68/payments incident timeline from 2026-11-23T15:58Z onward and correlate it with the retry queue depth, and have the owner of the checkout-service and payment-service instances confirm where those pods run, since neither name matches a workload in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable: traces_search for services checkout and payment returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span status, error count or CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span exists, and the checkout-to-payment edge is read from log text only, not from parent references.

Prometheus was unreachable: metrics_range_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout error rate, payment latency and any latency trend (no baseline could be compared) are unknown rather than zero.

Two pod-log error queries returned status no_data and prove nothing: fetch_pod_logs on checkout-6578865d87-v6flf for 2026-11-23T15:00:00Z-17:15:00Z with regex 'error|fail|timeout|circuit|unavailable|refused' matched 0 of 639 in-window lines, and on payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm for 15:00:00Z-17:58:00Z with regex 'error|fail|timeout|circuit|unavailable|adyen' matched 0 of 566 lines; absence of an error line in those pods is not established.

The events query over all namespaces returned status no_data with 0 items for the whole authorized window, so no controller or kubelet evidence of a rollout, eviction or restart mechanism exists; events expire and often carry null timestamps, so this is unknown rather than proof that nothing happened.

The external provider adyen-eu is not observable with the available sources; its degradation is asserted only by the log lines "payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)" and "adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page", and the status page itself could not be read.

Index coverage is thin (4 documents in 30 days), so the start of the 500s, their rate, and whether other services failed are unknown; the earliest index error is 15:58:18Z and the latest entry 17:28:18Z.

Pod stdout retention is limited: within the checkout and payment pods the log reads returned no previous container instance ("previous terminated container ... not found"), so the 15:58Z-16:58Z failure period and any recovery moment cannot be confirmed from pod logs.

The index service labels checkout-service and payment-service match no Deployment or Service in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 (which has checkout and payment), so the specific instances that returned the 500s remain unidentified.
The change-history integration is not registered, so whether a provider configuration or credential change preceded 15:58:18Z could not be checked, and secrets could not be read.
next_steps: Obtain the payment provider's incident and status-page record for adyen-eu /v68/payments on 2026-11-23 afternoon to confirm or refute the 30s-timeout origin.
Identify which deployment emits the service labels checkout-service and payment-service so their own error spans and metrics can be queried once Jaeger and Prometheus are reachable.

Once Prometheus is reachable, quantify the checkout PlaceOrder STATUS_CODE_ERROR ratio and payment client latency against a pre-15:58:18Z baseline and check the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert defined in the prometheus ConfigMap.

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
